question: Can causal patching localize and repair a prompt-format-dependent decimal-comparison error in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and does the evidence justify a general even/odd attention-head specialization mechanism?

key_findings.claim: The narrow behavioral phenomenon is reproducible within the paper's stated setup: identical decimal content changes answer quality across prompt formats.
key_findings.evidence: At temperature zero, the Q&A rendering of 'Which is bigger: 9.8 or 9.11?' is reported wrong in 1,000/1,000 trials, the simple rendering correct in 1,000/1,000, and the chat template wrong in 95%. A logit lens places overt answer divergence around layer 25, while attribution indicates earlier format differences. Because deterministic decoding repeats the same prompt, n=1,000 does not represent 1,000 independent model/data samples.

key_findings.claim: Attention-output transplantation at layer 10 is the paper's strongest causal result, whereas full-residual or single-head patching fails.
key_findings.evidence: Replacing full layer states from the working format produces incoherent text, and attention-only sweeps identify layer 10 as the sole reported perfect repair point. Forward transplantation from Simple to Q&A fixes the target output and reverse transplantation induces the error. This establishes necessity/sufficiency only for the chosen paired prompts, patch definition, and output criterion; it does not establish that native layer-10 attention alone caused the original learned bug across a task distribution.

key_findings.claim: The claimed universal parity rule and exact eight-head threshold are not supported by a consistent trial accounting in the paper.
key_findings.evidence: Section 4.1 says every subset of the 16 even heads and every subset of the 16 odd heads was tested for k=1..16 with 50 independent trials per combination. That entails 2*(2^16-1)*50 = 6,553,500 trials, and testing only the 12,870 eight-even-head subsets would entail 643,500. The limitations and conclusion instead describe just over 3,000 total trials. This irreconcilable mismatch prevents treating 'any eight even heads' or perfect redundancy as established without code/data reproduction.

key_findings.claim: Sparse-autoencoder correlations offer a hypothesis about format/numeric competition, not causal validation of the named features.
key_findings.evidence: Using Llama-Scope TopK SAEs, the paper reports numerical features correlated with even heads (mean r=0.89) and format features correlated with odd heads (r=0.86), plus 10% feature overlap at layer 7 and 80% at layer 10. The authors explicitly acknowledge reconstruction error, TopK omissions, and interpretation from activation patterns; no feature-level ablation establishes that the five named numerical features create the eight-head threshold.

key_findings.claim: Generalization evidence is too small and internally narrower than the paper's architectural language.
key_findings.evidence: Of five decimal pairs, only the canonical pair displays the target simple-correct/Q&A-wrong pattern; three are correct in both formats and the two-digit 10.9/10.11 case is not repaired. Appendix A tests other model families only ten times each and does not reproduce the parity mechanism. Thus the data support one Llama model/prompt pair, not the conclusion that transformers systematically organize content computation by head-index parity.

anchors.section: A Results with other models and Table 4

method.core_idea: Contrast working and failing prompt formats, localize representational divergence, and progressively change intervention granularity from full layers to attention outputs and head subsets.
method.mechanism: Run deterministic Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct prompts; inspect layerwise logits and attribution; transplant attention patterns between paired runs; sweep layers, replacement proportion, and even/odd head subsets; correlate outcomes with pretrained Llama-Scope SAE features.
assumptions: Patched activations remain on a meaningful causal manifold despite coming from differently tokenized/formatted prompts.
Binary correctness of one generated answer is a sufficient intervention metric.
Repeated deterministic executions can be treated as independent trials for confidence intervals.
SAE feature labels and correlations identify the computations performed by the corresponding heads.

techniques.role: Transplants residual or attention states from a working prompt into a failing prompt.
Searches which layer-10 attention-head subsets can change the answer.
Locates when working and failing formats diverge in output preference.
Associates prompt-format and numerical-comparison feature activations with the intervention site.

evaluations.setting: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on 9.8 versus 9.11 under Q&A, simple, and chat renderings
evaluations.baseline: same semantic question in the alternate prompt formats

evaluations.setting: Cross-format activation patching over layers and submodules
evaluations.result: reported 100% only for layer-10 attention-output replacement; full layers, MLP-only, individual heads, and neighboring layers fail

evaluations.setting: Five decimal pairs and six model families
evaluations.result: the exact target failure/repair generalizes to no additional decimal pair in Table 3; model-level error rates vary in ten-run appendix tests

limitations: The central mechanism is evaluated in one model on essentially one decimal pair.
The stated exhaustive subset experiment is mathematically inconsistent with the reported total trial count.
Temperature-zero repeats of one prompt are not independent statistical samples.
SAE features are correlational and were not causally ablated.
No task-level side-effect evaluation checks whether the repair damages other numerical, linguistic, or safety behaviors.
Several numerical descriptions conflict internally, including chat error rates and layer-25 token probabilities.
failure_modes: Cross-format patching can create incoherent off-manifold activations rather than reveal a native circuit.
Head parity may be an artifact of indexing, grouped-query implementation, or a coding bug in head selection.
A repair tuned to a fixed tokenization can fail on multi-digit numbers or paraphrases.
Binary output scoring can hide probability shifts, calibration damage, or alternative valid phrasings.
SAE reconstruction and feature splitting can make a neat five-feature threshold appear even when underlying computation is distributed.
reusable_insights: Intervention granularity should be swept explicitly; layer-, sublayer-, head-, and feature-level patches answer different causal questions.
Bidirectional patching is stronger than a one-way repair because it tests whether the candidate state can both fix and induce behavior.
Before interpreting combinatorial sweeps, reconcile the number of configurations, trials, and reported compute exactly.
Mechanistic claims should generalize across prompts and tokenizations before being elevated to architectural principles.
open_questions: Can an independent reproduction recover the parity pattern after auditing head-index and grouped-query-attention code?
Does the eight-head threshold persist over a preregistered distribution of decimal comparisons and paraphrases?
What collateral effects follow from permanently editing or steering the identified attention outputs?
Do feature-level causal interventions reproduce the claimed five-feature threshold?
How should patching experiments account for mismatched token positions and off-manifold states across formats?

competitive_landscape.title: Does Circuit Analysis Interpretability Scale? Evidence from Multiple Choice Capabilities in Chinchilla
competitive_landscape.difference: Lieberum et al. use resampling ablations and causal-graph accounting across prompt distributions in Chinchilla; this paper focuses on cross-format pattern transplantation for one failure and claims a much sharper head-parity rule.

competitive_landscape.title: AtP*: An Efficient and Scalable Method for Localizing LLM Behaviour to Components
competitive_landscape.difference: AtP* approximates causal attribution and validates candidates with activation patching across distributions; this paper performs direct exhaustive-looking layer/head interventions but lacks coherent configuration accounting and broad prompts.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpreting Attention Layer Outputs with Sparse Autoencoders
competitive_landscape.difference: Kissane et al. train attention-output SAEs across several model families and find most heads polysemantic; this paper uses residual-stream Llama-Scope features to argue for binary even/odd specialization in one layer and task.

competitive_landscape.title: Llama Scope: Extracting Millions of Features from Llama-3.1-8B with Sparse Autoencoders
competitive_landscape.relationship: Enabling SAE resource and methodological baseline
competitive_landscape.difference: Llama Scope supplies the pretrained TopK SAEs and documents feature splitting, reconstruction, and transfer behavior; the reviewed paper applies those checkpoints to a specific decimal-format contrast and adds unsupported causal labels to correlated features.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: A precise layer-10 attention repair reveals universal even/odd head specialization, perfect redundancy among 16 even heads, and sharp eight-head and 60% phase transitions.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper reports bidirectional layer-10 pattern transplantation, layer/granularity sweeps, parity-group interventions, and SAE correlations on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Cross-format sublayer patching of the canonical decimal error is a useful case study. The headline parity, redundancy, and architectural claims are not reliable as written because combinatorial trial counts contradict the paper's totals, independent samples are absent, and generalization beyond one pair/model is not demonstrated.

reviewer_notes: Read all 19 pages and explicitly audited internal arithmetic and cross-section consistency. Primary-source competitor records were checked on 2026-08-23. This record intentionally distinguishes the potentially useful layer-10 patching observation from the paper's substantially overgeneralized and internally inconsistent parity claims.
